headline: Open-source software tools for single-cell, genome browser, and synteny analyses
label: Genomic Data Analysis Tools
summary: Recent preprints release open tools for single-cell annotation, genome browser track translation, and BLAST-based synteny and ortholog analysis across species.
synthesis: The three preprints share a focus on software infrastructure that makes comparative and cross-species genomic workflows more accessible, including for non-model organisms. SAPTICoN provides a no-code, reproducible Snakemake/Seurat pipeline for single-cell transcriptomics that auto-generates annotation packages for non-model species. Track Hub Quickload Translator converts bidirectionally between UCSC Track Hub and Integrated Genome Browser Quickload formats, enabling access to about 50,000 GenArk genomes within IGB. Novabrowse interprets BLAST results through multi-species synteny analysis, ortholog detection, and gene signal discovery. The novelty lies in interoperability across analysis ecosystems rather than in a new biological finding. The items do not report benchmarks against one another, so no performance comparison is implied.
